note: Spoken, not read: talking to a friend at full pace. Asides (honestly?, okay so, yep), a run-on here and there, the narrator voicing the brain's panic (wait- are we falling?!), speed changes by meaning (hushed start, fast jolt, quick explanation, punchy payoff). Per phrase: speed, tone (low/mid/high pitch placement), end (rise/fall), emph, pause after, breath before, gain; alts = punctuation variants auditioned too.

segments.t: You're just drifting off...
and then—
your whole body jumps!
Yeah... you're not imagining it.
It's called a hypnic jerk,
and honestly? It's super common.
Okay, so what's actually going on?
alts: Okay so... what's actually going on?

segments.t: As you fall asleep, your brain waves slow way down,
and your muscles just... go loose.
But scientists think that sometimes,
your brain notices all that relaxing...
and totally misreads it.
Like, wait— are we falling?!
So it slams the panic button!
A burst of signals shoots down your spine,
and boom— your muscles all fire at once.
alts: and boom, your muscles all fire at once.

segments.t: That's why it feels so real.
Like you tripped, or stepped off a ledge.
Sometimes your brain even throws in a quick falling dream, just to match.
So next time you kick yourself awake...
yep, that's just your brain, hitting the panic button...
alts: yep. That's just your brain, hitting the panic button...

segments.t: for absolutely no reason.
